title: Java Introduction
summary: Meet Java with three tiny programs. Print a greeting, add pencil counts and ask a simple yes-or-no question about a score.
introduction: A program is a list of steps for a computer. Java is one language you can use to write those steps. People use it for apps and large computer systems. We will begin with a greeting and a little maths. You do not need to remember every new symbol at once.
learningObjectives: Use if to make a simple choice

rows: A name for a stored value, such as a pencil count.
A type for whole numbers, such as 3 or 10.
The tool kit used to build and run Java code.

blocks.title: Where to run the examples
blocks.text: Read the [setup lesson](/tutorials/java/setup-jdk) to use Java on your computer. These examples are shown here for reading; they do not run in this site playground.
The main method is where this program starts. System.out.println shows a value and starts a new line. Save each example as Main.java, one at a time.

blocks.title: Main.java

blocks.text: int tells Java that pencils is a whole number. The plus sign adds the two counts before the result is printed.

blocks.title: Main.java

blocks.text: if checks a rule. The >= sign means greater than or equal to. A score of 8 passes this check, so the message appears.

blocks.title: Main.java
Watch out
blocks.text: Java and JavaScript are different languages. Use the Java tools from the setup lesson. Keep Main.java and the class name Main spelled the same way.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Change 3 pencils to 6 in the second program. Predict the total, then run it.
